results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

results.quote: At Veldmark that shared rule became the June ranking policy: a month after the forum it capped paid positions on the first page and withdrew "Spotlight" altogether, making Proposal 1's deferral final
results.finding: Both flow readers found the end of Proposal 1's story out of place in the general Trade-offs section: it reopens the worked example after it has closed, jumps a month forward and overtakes the 'deferred' verdict just read; 'withdrew' also suggests Spotlight had launched (reader-flow-a item 15: 'This was the clearest out-of-place moment'). The spec places this outcome in p68, so the difficulty comes from the declared order; moving it to Proposal 1's decision (and saying 'ruled out' rather than 'withdrew') would fix it.

results.quote: Both are covered above: a naive package comparison makes sales teams discount the products that work best
results.finding: A failure-mode entry that only points back breaks the parallel list (each other entry states a failure and its remedy); reader-flow-a item 17 stopped to check nothing new was said, reader-flow-b called it 'like a placeholder'. The spec's p75 declares the paragraph as 'covered above', so the fault is the spec's unit.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What a Listing Marketplace Sells ¶7
results.quote: Lead-generation portals (Zillow) report revenue per unit of audience.
results.finding: Both readers stumbled on why a lead-generation portal's KPI is revenue per visit (the table row) and how it fits 'per unit of audience'; the text never says why a lead-gen business uses an audience denominator (reader-flow-a item 4: 'Why a lead-gen business reports per visit is not explained').

results.quote: The cause of the volume loss is not covered by the sources used here.
results.finding: The Hemnet evidence gives revenue per listing up and net sales down but never states that listing volume fell, then refers to 'the volume loss' as if stated and leaves it as a loose end until p28a (reader-flow-a item 7: 'The text never says that listing volume fell'). One sentence saying the falling net sales despite rising yield means fewer listings would close it.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Revenue Mix and Three Proposals ¶8 and ¶11
results.quote: the Keybridge decision of March 2027 forbids Hearthly from using Keybridge agency data for sales targeting
results.finding: The worked example claims to answer Ingrid's four questions, but only Proposal 1 answers all four; Proposal 2 drops 'Who notices first' and Proposal 3 replaces liquidity cost and who-notices-first with 'New systems' and 'Governance cost', so the reader returning to the scene's test cannot follow it (reader-flow-b item 8: 'the worked example does not follow them consistently'). The spec's p62 and p65 do not declare the four answers for Proposals 2 and 3, unlike p59, so the gap is in the spec. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What a Listing Marketplace Sells ¶2
results.quote: Charging the demand side is the exception, and it works only where supply is scarce. Scout24's ImmoScout24 sells consumer "Plus" subscriptions to renters and buyers.
results.finding: Reader-flow-a item 1: the first detailed evidence in Concepts is model 10 (consumer subscriptions) before the models exist, and model 10 later only points back ('as ImmoScout24 Plus shows above'). The spec places this evidence in p07. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Revenue Mix and Three Proposals ¶3
results.quote: Spread across the cars its dealers list, Motorvane's ARPA shows where its revenue is exposed: the slot.
results.finding: Reader-flow-b item 6: the sentence needed a re-read and the slot-value paragraph reads like a sidebar under the revenue mix, since its only use is the comparison in Proposal 2 (€15 slot vs €228 lead fees). The spec deliberately puts it in the revenue mix (worked-example flow rationale). Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What a Listing Marketplace Sells ¶4
results.quote: Every model spends liquidity on behalf of a paying side, so the next question is what that side is charged for.
results.finding: Reader-flow-b item 2: the bridge asserts a causal link that does not hold (spending liquidity does not lead to the unit-of-charge question), so the reader re-read it looking for the connection. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What a Listing Marketplace Sells ¶6
results.quote: The table names three KPIs whose definitions recur in this part of the book.
results.finding: Reader-flow-a item 3: the table shows seven KPIs, and only the following sentences reveal which three are meant; the reader re-scanned the table. Naming the three in this sentence would fix it. Single reader.

results.draft_locus: Architecture: The Systems Each Model Requires ¶3
results.quote: In the matrix, catalog and pricing, entitlements, ranking hooks and metering serve most models, so they form one shared core.
results.finding: Reader-flow-a item 10: in the matrix, ranking hooks and delivery metering are marked for only about half the models, so 'serve most models' did not match the table and the reader checked it again. Single reader.
